svg.title: The Christmas ghost story, step by step: a boy's sad winter tale in The Winter's Tale, Dickens's ghost story of Christmas in 1843, Jerome's joke in 1891 and M. R. James's collection of 1904.
svg.desc: A vertical timeline of four entries. Act 2 of The Winter's Tale: a boy says a sad tale is best for winter and offers one of sprites and goblins. 1843: Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol, Being a Ghost Story of Christmas, on 19 December. 1891: Jerome K. Jerome jokes in Told After Supper that it always is Christmas Eve in a ghost story. 1904: M. R. James's Ghost Stories of an Antiquary is published; he read such tales aloud as Christmas Eve entertainments.
svg.text: The Christmas ghost story, step by step
In The Winter's Tale a boy says a sad tale is best for
winter and offers one of sprites and goblins.
Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol on 19 December,
'Being a Ghost Story of Christmas'; 6,000 copies sold by the 24th.
Jerome K. Jerome jokes in Told After Supper that it
'always is Christmas Eve, in a ghost story'.
M. R. James's Ghost Stories of an Antiquary appears;
he read such tales aloud as Christmas Eve entertainments.
